title: Character and temperament
note: Several of these hide a trap: punctilious is not punctual, urbane is not urban, callow is not callous, and officious is not official. The old theory of four bodily humors left us phlegmatic (calm), choleric (angry), sanguine (hopeful) and melancholy.

items.ex: The irascible landlord shouted at anyone who parked near his hedge.

items.a: calm and slow to show emotion
items.ex: Even when the engine caught fire, the phlegmatic pilot spoke in a level voice.

items.a: prone to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood
d: calm and slow to show emotion
items.ex: Her mercurial boss could praise a draft at noon and shred it by two.
The dour inspector found fault with everything, including the weather.

items.a: friendly and easy to talk to
items.ex: The affable new neighbor knew everyone's name within a week.

items.a: eager to fight or argue; aggressively defiant
items.ex: Questioned about the missing funds, the treasurer turned truculent.
The obstreperous crowd drowned out the speaker by the second minute.
With both sides intransigent, the talks collapsed before lunch.

items.a: shy from a lack of self-confidence
items.ex: The diffident student had the best answer but never raised her hand.
He gave an insouciant shrug as the deadline sailed past.
The imperturbable referee ignored the jeers and blew the whistle.
She stayed stoic through the long rehab and never once asked for pity.
The ebullient host hugged every guest at the door.
It seemed churlish to refuse a gift offered with such care.
The pusillanimous council postponed the vote rather than face the crowd.
An intrepid reporter walked into the flood zone to get the story.

items.a: boldly daring; willing to take risks
items.ex: The audacious plan called for crossing the desert in winter.
The indefatigable volunteer knocked on four hundred doors in a weekend.
The indolent cat moved only to follow the patch of sunlight.

items.a: meddlesome, pushing unwanted help or advice
items.ex: An officious clerk rewrote my form even though it was correct.

items.a: excessively eager to please or obey
items.ex: The obsequious waiter laughed at every one of the director's jokes.
She gave my thrift-store coat a supercilious glance.
The urbane diplomat smoothed over the insult with a joke in three languages.

items.a: strictly attentive to correct conduct and detail
items.ex: A punctilious editor, he checked every comma against the style guide.
His feckless nephew borrowed the truck and returned it empty and dented.

d: old and set in one's ways
items.ex: The callow intern promised the client a deadline no one could meet.

items.a: kind and friendly, like an uncle
d: stern and strict, like a drill sergeant
items.ex: The avuncular professor kept a jar of candy for students in office hours.
The feud survived three generations of implacable grudges.
His cavalier attitude toward safety rules finally cost him the job.
A timorous knock came at the door, then a long silence.
